html:
The Acaxee were a Native American people of the Sierra Madre Occidental where Durango meets Sinaloa, in northern Mexico. They lived in scattered villages on the steep slopes, farming maize and beans.

Spanish silver mines opened in their mountains in the late 1500s, around Topia and San Andrés. In 1601 a native prophet led the Acaxee in a revolt against the miners and missionaries. The governor of Nueva Vizcaya put it down with the help of Jesuit go-betweens, and the Acaxee were gathered into mission towns. Disease then shrank them fast, and they disappear as a people in the 1700s. Their neighbours were the Xixime and the Tepehuán, in New Spain.
